Pro
PROH
noun / adjective (Gen Alpha slang)
Clipped from professional, in sporting use since the nineteenth century (a "pro" as opposed to an amateur). Gaming culture of the 2000s–2020s made "pro" the highest praise for skill — esports professionals, "pro players," and the meme "pro gamer move" for a clever (often sneaky) trick. For Gen Alpha, "pro" is simply the opposite of "noob": "He’s a pro at Fortnite," "I’m pro at this," and "pro" as an adjective for anything done skillfully.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In Gen Alpha talk a pro is someone very good at something — especially a game. Calling yourself "pro" is a boast; calling a friend "pro" is a compliment. The Christian observation: skill is a gift of God, and Scripture praises it. The Psalmist says to "play skilfully with a loud noise" (Psa 33:3), and Bezaleel’s craftsmanship came from the Spirit of God. Work done with excellence honors the Lord: "whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men" (Col 3:23); "Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might" (Ecc 9:10). So it is good to want to be a pro. But Scripture also keeps a child humble about his skill: "For who maketh thee to differ from another? and what hast thou that thou didst not receive?" (1Co 4:7), and a man should not "think of himself more highly than he ought to think" (Rom 12:3). And it asks what we are getting good at. A child who is a pro at Fortnite and a beginner at kindness has practiced in the wrong order. A father can tell a five-year-old: "God made you able to get really good at things — that’s a gift from Him! Let’s get to be pros at loving people and helping, too." The best pro is the one who says thank you to the Giver.

Webster 1828 Definition

Clip of professional (19th-c. sport; gaming 2000s-) — Gen Alpha’s word for skill, a gift Scripture praises when it is done heartily unto the Lord and held humbly as received.

PRO, n. / a. (clip of professional; gaming usage 2000s–present; Gen Alpha) A highly skilled player; skillful. "She’s pro at Minecraft."

Pro gamer move — meme phrase for a clever or sneaky trick.

Opposite: noob, bot, default.

Decode for parents: a harmless compliment, sometimes a boast.

Webster 1828, the root — PROFESSIONAL, a. Pertaining to a profession or to a calling; as professional studies, pursuits, duties, engagements; professional character or skill.

Key Scripture

Psa 33:3 — "Sing unto him a new song; play skilfully with a loud noise."

Col 3:23 — "And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;"

Ecc 9:10 — "Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest."

1Co 4:7 — "For who maketh thee to differ from another? and what hast thou that thou didst not receive? now if thou didst receive it, why dost thou glory, as if thou hadst not received it?"

Rom 12:3 — "For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith."

Modern Corruption

"Pro" praises real skill, which is God’s gift; it turns sour only as a boast, or when a child is a pro at the trivial and a beginner at the weighty.

expand to see more

There is little to correct in a word that praises excellence. The temptation is pride: the pro who looks down on the noob, the boast that forgets the gift. A secondary danger is disordered practice — the hours that make a child a pro at a game while the skills of home, school, and church go untended.

Praise excellence and ask what it serves. Teach the child to do everything heartily as to the Lord, to thank God for the ability, and to help the beginner. A pro who teaches a noob is living Romans 12.
